_comment: CFD prop-firm profile: trades CFDs via MetaTrader 5 across one or more prop-firm accounts. Forecast is generated ONCE for all accounts; per-account sizing uses each account's live balance/equity from MT5. Credentials are env-var NAMES only -- real values live in .env (gitignored).

data._comment: Historical data fetched via IB (TWS) for price quality consistency with prop/personal profiles. MT5 is execution-only in v1. Could switch to MT5 data later via 'source': 'mt5'.

mt5._comment_magic: Magic number ranges identify OUR orders so we never touch positions opened by other strategies/manual trades on the same account. Each account should have a unique magic_number; default_magic_number is used when an account omits it.

accounts._comment: Example FTMO 50K demo account. Replace label, magic_number, and env var names per your setup. The env vars listed below must be set in your environment (or .env) before running with --execute.
accounts.label: ftmo_50k_demo_a

execution._comment_approval: Default-on-timeout 'cancel' is the conservative choice. To enable 'no answer in 5 min = execute', set default_on_timeout to 'approve'. Even with 'approve', a Telegram/network outage detected during polling will still cancel (fail-closed).
execution._comment_authorized: authorized_telegram_user_ids is a whitelist of numeric Telegram user IDs allowed to approve/cancel. Leave empty + set allow_any_approver=false to fail-closed during initial setup. To find your user ID, DM @userinfobot in Telegram.
execution._comment_sizing: min_rebalance_lots is a hard floor in lots (never trade less). min_rebalance_notional_usd is a dead-band on the dollar value of the delta (skip noise). rebalance_mode: hybrid_close_on_flip is described in docs/library/live_forecast/cfd_prop_workflow.md.
execution._comment_safety: Optional preflight gates. max_spread_points caps acceptable spread; max_margin_usage_pct prevents margin-call risk; max_daily_loss_pct enforces prop-firm DLL.
execution._comment_audit: Per-run JSON audit log directory (created if missing). Each run writes one file with plans + decisions + execution results for post-mortem analysis.
